title: Integer to Roman
hints: Greedy: always use the largest value that still fits.
Keep an ordered array of `(value, symbol)` pairs that includes the subtractive pairs like 900 = "CM".
`result += String(repeating: symbol, count: n / value); n %= value`.
jsBridge: An ordered array of `(value, symbol)` tuples drives a greedy loop. The JS version is identical with arrays of pairs. Swift tuples with labels (`(value: 900, symbol: "CM")`) read better and cost nothing.

compass.q: JS: `[[1000,'M'],…]`. Swift: `[(value: Int, symbol: String)]`. What do labels buy you?
Why must this be an array, not a dictionary? (Order.)
What's the reverse (Roman → Int) trick with the subtractive pairs?
Foundation can't format Roman numerals, but `NumberFormatter` does spell-out. When would an app need either?
